source_excerpts.text:
## The construction: acquire a representation together with an order of queries that preserves it

I moved to **exact probabilistic inference in networks of small local factors**. The central obstacle is independent of our earlier representation: even when every factor has only eight entries, loops can make counting, conditioning and sampling expensive. A compact transformed representation may make the partition function easy while leaving the original-variable queries needed for sampling difficult.

I built a mechanism that addresses that second problem:

> **Discover compatible local coordinates, then construct an observation order that keeps every required conditional calculation inside a tractable planar class. The internal coordinates may contain negative values; the sampler still returns exact samples of the original positive distribution.**

The work produced three connected results:

- An explicit invariant for recognizing compatible parity coordinates in the generic ternary case, with actual basis reconstruction from the supplied tables.
- A broader theorem showing how to close exposed boundaries of planar matchgate networks without expanding their exponentially large boundary tensors.
- An executed exact counter, weighted unranking procedure and original-variable sampler, alongside a conventional bucket-elimination sampler.

The conventional implementation is faster on the small meshes I tested. I have established the construction and its guarantees, rather than a practical speed advantage or external priority for the combination.

The earlier input-effect subspace, original-input consumers, coNP-complete admission theorem and solver-free rejection checker remain preserved, including the previous comparator’s contribution of the short rejection certificate.

## 1. The problem being solved

Let a plane graph \(G=(V,E)\) carry a binary variable \(x_e\) on each edge. At vertex \(v\), an explicitly supplied table \(f_v\) assigns a weight to the incident edge values. The original distribution is

\[
W(x)=\prod_{v\in V} f_v(x_{\partial v}),
\qquad
Z=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{E}}W(x),
\qquad
\pi(x)=\frac{W(x)}{Z}.
\]

The implemented acquisition procedure starts with ternary factors: each vertex has three incident variables, and each table contains eight rational numbers. Its executed sampling cases have strictly positive original tables.

source_excerpts.text:
The implementation now includes:

Raw-table decomposition and exact reconstruction.
Vertex compatibility invariants.
Construction of compatible edge bases.
Field extraction and sign correction.
Face-cover acquisition and observation-order construction.
Signed planar counting.
Exact original-variable weighted unranking and sampling.
Conventional min-fill elimination with retained reverse conditionals.

The most informative completed checks were:

Check	Executed result
Signed Pfaffian elimination against independent recursive expansion	150 matrices
Signed boundary-product Pfaffian identity	192 cases, boundary arity up to 10
Actual weighted parity matchgate signatures	252 cases, including zero and negative weights
Even/odd parity-chain assignments	16,382
Exhaustive original-variable prefixes, signed-coordinate example	127
Exhaustive original-variable prefixes, quadratic-coordinate example	127
Endpoints of weighted unranking intervals	128
Random evidence sets checked against exact elimination	48

Among those 48 evidence checks, 36 used a one-face cover and 12 used a two-face cover. A separate example with three initial field sites used a two-face base cover and had maximum prefix cover size two.

I also tested acquisition on 256 independently generated positive eight-entry tables. After extending the arithmetic, 202 admitted the local decomposition handled by the recognizer. That is a local-decomposition result, not a claim that 202 random networks became tractable. Compatibility, field placement and arithmetic across a whole network still matter.

The conventional route is strong

The comparison retains exact bucket conditionals and samples in reverse elimination order. It does not rerun a full elimination for each sampled bit.

For a 16-factor, 24-variable signed-coordinate case, representative executed times were approximately:

Operation	Acquired boundary method	Conventional bucket elimination
Acquire coordinates	0.010 s	—
Compile all prefix topologies / compile bucket conditionals	0.139 s	0.0040 s
Draw one original-variable sample	0.351 s	0.000058 s

Both gave exactly the same partition function. The conventional sampler’s complete probability formula was also checked against every original assignment in the six-variable cases.
